sources.title: Copom Selic decisions 2026 (cut to 13.75% on 16 Sep 2026; next meeting 4 Nov)
Nu officially launches as a licensed bank in Mexico (6 Aug 2026)
Brazil extends exemptions for IoT, increases taxation on fintechs
Central bank resolutions limiting unsolicited credit marketing from 2027 (23 Oct 2026), as reported in secondary coverage

notes: mc GEOGRAPHY FY2025 revenue (20-F note 34b, non-current assets = ROU, PP&E, intangibles, goodwill): Brazil 91.3% (11,038.3 of 12,083.8), Mexico 6.7%, other (Colombia etc.) 2.0%; non-current assets Brazil 80.4%, Mexico 5.7%, other 13.9%. Mexico revenue grew 54% in 2025 (523.1 to 808.1). No customer is 10% of revenue [pf_10k_20260408].

mc EXPOSURE Brazil Selic and funding: Selic 15.00% at the 20-F date (peak 15% since 18 Jun 2025); cut to 14.25% (Jun 2026), 14.00% (Aug), 13.75% (16 Sep 2026); next Copom 4 Nov 2026; Focus survey of 13 Oct expects 13.25% by year-end (attributed expectation, not a fact). Nu's deposits are remunerated at SELIC-linked rates and payroll loans use SELIC as benchmark [pf_10k_20260408, mc_bcb_selic]. Sensitivity sizing from the 20-F market-risk table is left to the analyst (hypothesis until sized).

mc EXPOSURE Brazil tax: Complementary Law 224 (Dec 2025) raises CSLL for certain financial companies to 17.5% from Apr 2026 through Dec 2027 and 20% from Jan 2028 (non-financial 12% then 15%); IRPJ 25%; PIS/COFINS to be replaced by VAT from 2027 on a multi-year transition [pf_10k_20260408, mc_bnam_fintech_tax]. Applies to roughly 91% of revenue (Brazil share) so it is a sized bear mechanism on Brazil net margin; the exact share of Nu entities subject to 17.5%/20% vs lower rates is a gap. Nu announced (Jul 2026, secondary coverage) a bank licence purchase in Brazil (Banco Porto Real): bank status would put it under bank tax rules (hypothesis, unconfirmed at primary source). IOF: no 2026 IOF rise aimed at fintechs found; 2025 decrees widened IOF on credit/FX (not sized).

mc EXPOSURE Brazil credit quality: BCB household default on market-rate credit 8.09% in Sep 2026 vs 8.03% Aug and 6.89% Sep 2025, the highest of the series since Mar 2011 (published 29 Oct 2026, via secondary coverage) [mc_rt_default]. Same direction as Nu's consumer book (cards, personal and payroll loans); Nu's own NPL ratios are for gather_numbers/documents.

mc EXPOSURE Brazil politics, fiscal, FX: Lula won the 25 Oct 2026 runoff 51.8% to 48.2% over Flavio Bolsonaro; BRL fell about 10.5-12% intraday to around 5.60 per USD, then recovered to about 5.36; iShares MSCI Brazil ETF reported down ~25% premarket on 26 Oct; Bolsonaro reportedly challenged the result in court, outcome confirmed by the electoral court; analysts flag persistent primary deficits and rising public debt [mc_cnbc_election, mc_aljaz_real]. Reaction sizes differ between sources; a Nu share-price move is not confirmed at primary source here (gather_numbers owns price). FX translation: about 91% of revenue is in BRL, reporting is in USD, so BRL level maps directly into USD revenue and book value (hypothesis for sizing).

mc EXPOSURE Mexico: 6.7% of FY2025 revenue (growing). CNBV/SHCP final authorization 9-10 Jul 2026 and launch as a full bank on 6 Aug 2026 (from a Sofipo), enabling payroll accounts and broader credit; deposits now IPAB-insured; >15 million customers; plan to invest US$4.2 billion in Mexico through 2030 (company statements, via secondary coverage) [mc_6k_20260710, mc_rt_nubank_mx]. Mexico average CETES 28-day 8.11% in 2025, MXN average 19.2 per USD in 2025 vs 18.3 in 2024; USMCA is up for review in 2026 per risk factors [pf_10k_20260408]. Higher capital and liquidity requirements as a bank not sized (gap).

mc EXPOSURE Brazil regulation: central bank resolutions of 23 Oct 2026 restrict unsolicited credit marketing from 2027, a customer-acquisition and credit-limit-increase exposure (secondary coverage, not read at the BCB source, not sized) [mc_rt_bcb_marketing]. Tariffs: no company-specific exposure; the 20-F only names general US tariff and USMCA uncertainty. No export-control, Taiwan or sanctions exposure applies to a Latin American digital bank.

mc NEWS 2026-10-23 6-K: CTO Eric Young resigns (stays to 12 Nov 2026); founder-CEO David Velez oversees Global Platforms, CISO John Walton interim co-lead; permanent CTO search started; strategy said unchanged [mc_6k_20261023]. Citable from 2026-10-25.
mc NEWS 2026-10-25/26 Lula re-elected in runoff; BRL and Brazilian equities sold off sharply, partial recovery by 27 Oct (see EXPOSURE politics) [mc_cnbc_election, mc_aljaz_real].

mc NEWS 2026-10-29 BCB credit statistics for September: household default record 8.09% [mc_rt_default]. 6-Ks of 2026-09-30, 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-02 were not opened (headers have no items; likely routine notices): gap. Q3 2026 results not yet released at as_of; the Q2 results (2026-08-13, record net income US$1.1 billion per press) are the latest and are gather_documents' lane.

mc RATES market block: risk-free 4.98% (FRED DGS10, 2026-10-29) and ERP 4.20% (Damodaran implied, 2026-10-01) kept from the prefetch; Damodaran's 1 Nov update was not yet checkable as of the cutoff. Brazil country-risk row is built from the geography facts above.
